title: Universal Drude Weights in One-dimensional Repulsive Fermi Gas
authors: Xiangguo Yin, Dawei Niu, Shuang Zhang, Shizhong Zhang, Yunbo Zhang, Xi-Wen Guan
abstract: Building on the Bethe ansatz and generalized hydrodynamics, we rigorously establish universal relations between Drude weights governing charge, spin, and energy transport and thermodynamic properties for the one-dimensional repulsive two-component continuum Fermi gas - the paradigmatic integrable Yang-Gaudin model. We analytically derive thermodynamic expressions for charge Drude weights: $D_{nn}$, $D_{nm}$, $D_{ne}$ (responses of particle, magnetization and energy currents to a chemical potential gradient) equal the particle density, magnetization, and temperature times entropy density, respectively. These relations constitute a hallmark of ballistic transport, and can be generalized to other 1D continuum integrable systems. Furthermore, we investigate spin Drude weight ($D_{mm}$, $D_{me}$) at zero and low temperatures. They characterize the magnetization and energy current responses to a magnetic field gradient, revealing an essential spin-charge coupling feature in quantum transport. We find that the Drude weights $D_{nm}$, $D_{mm}$, and $D_{me}$ across the $μ\text{-}H$ plane remarkably map out the zero-temperature phase boundary. This work fills a critical gap in the understanding of transport within integrable quantum gases and furnishes a direct theoretical foundation for future ultracold-atom experiments.
summary: This paper derives universal, exact relations for the Drude weights characterizing charge, spin, and energy transport in the 1D repulsive Fermi gas (Yang-Gaudin model). Using advanced techniques like generalized hydrodynamics, the authors confirm that charge transport is purely ballistic and relate these weights directly to fundamental thermodynamic quantities. This provides a crucial theoretical benchmark for experiments with ultracold atoms.
main_problem: To rigorously establish universal relations between Drude weights governing charge, spin, and energy transport and thermodynamic properties in the 1D repulsive two-component continuum Fermi gas.
main_result: The charge Drude weights are shown to equal the particle density, magnetization, and entropy density, confirming ballistic transport. Furthermore, the spin Drude weights map out the zero-temperature phase boundary across the mu-H plane.
method: The work builds upon the Bethe ansatz and generalized hydrodynamics (GHD), utilizing rapidity-space formulations and integral equations to derive transport coefficients.
model_or_system: The system is the one-dimensional (1D) repulsive two-component continuum Fermi gas, modeled by the integrable Yang-Gaudin model, which is a paradigmatic system for studying interacting quantum gases.
key_observables: Drude Weights ($D_{nn}, D_{mm}, D_{ne}, D_{me}$), particle density ($n$), magnetization ($m_z$), and entropy density ($s$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and magnetic field ($H$). The analysis explores zero and low-temperature limits.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the system being described by the Yang-Gaudin model and utilizes advanced theoretical frameworks like GHD and TBA equations.
figures_summary: Figures compare calculated Drude weights from different theoretical protocols (integral form, tilted potential, partitioning) against each other and against numerical results, confirming consistency.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the transport coefficients by relating them to derivatives of thermodynamic potentials in the grand canonical ensemble, confirming the ballistic nature of charge and spin transport while treating energy transport separately.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical foundation for understanding transport in integrable quantum gases, directly relevant to ultracold atom experiments where such systems are realized.
